title: How do you run a training gap analysis?
seoTitle: How to run a training gap analysis
description: How to run a training gap analysis against a fixed standard: baseline, decompose, inventory, compare, classify five gap types, rate severity and remediate.
shortAnswer: A training gap analysis is run by fixing the standard to compare against and its version, breaking it into testable requirements, taking an inventory of current training, assessment and records, comparing the two requirement by requirement, classifying each gap as coverage, depth, currency, evidence or population, rating severity by consequence, and producing a remediation plan with owners and dates.
keyTakeaways: A gap analysis compares current state against a fixed, versioned standard. Without a named standard there is nothing to measure against.
Classify gaps by type. Missing content, shallow content, outdated content, missing evidence and missing people each need a different fix.
Severity should be driven by the consequence of the requirement not being met, not by how much work the fix is.
The output is a gap register with owners and dates, not a narrative report.
Re-run the comparison after remediation to close each gap with evidence.

sections.heading: What is a training gap analysis and how is it different from a TNA?

blocks.text: A training gap analysis compares what an organization's training, assessment and records currently cover against a defined standard, and lists the differences. A [training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis) asks the wider question of whether and what training is needed to solve a performance problem.

In practice a gap analysis is usually triggered by a change in the standard: a regulation commences, a regulator issues guidance, an accreditation standard is revised, or an audit finds a weakness. Australia's AML/CTF reforms are an example. AUSTRAC states that changes to AML/CTF program requirements for current reporting entities started on 31 March 2026 unless deferred under the transitional rules, and that newly regulated services are regulated from 1 July 2026 ([AUSTRAC](https://www.austrac.gov.au/industry-and-business/about-amlctf-reforms/about-reforms)). Each change like that calls for a fresh comparison. The [comparison page](/compare/training-needs-analysis-vs-gap-analysis) sets out the two methods side by side.

sections.heading: What types of training gap are there?

blocks.text: There are five types, and each needs a different remedy. Classifying gaps by type stops every finding from being answered with 'build a new course'.

blocks.caption: Five types of training gap
head: Gap type
What it means
Typical remedy
rows: Coverage
A requirement is not addressed by any training or assessment
Design new outcome, content and assessment
Depth
The requirement is addressed, but at a lower level than the role needs (for example awareness where application is required)
Rewrite outcomes at the right level and replace knowledge checks with applied assessment
Currency
Content reflects an earlier version of the standard or procedure
Update content and re-issue to affected roles
Evidence
Training exists but there is no record, or the record shows attendance not achievement
Add assessment and fix record keeping
Population
Training is right but not everyone who needs it has done it, including contractors or people who changed role
Fix assignment rules in the training matrix and chase completion

sections.heading: What are the steps in a training gap analysis?

blocks.text: There are eight steps. Steps one to three define both sides of the comparison; steps four to six are the comparison; seven and eight turn findings into action.

items: **Fix the reference standard.** Name the instrument, guidance or internal policy and the exact version or date. Output: a baseline statement, for example 'AUSTRAC AML/CTF training guidance as published on the date of review'.
**Decompose it into testable requirements.** Break the standard into statements that can each be answered met, partly met or not met. Output: a requirements list, each with a source reference.

**Take an inventory of the current state.** List training modules, their outcomes and versions, assessment instruments, assignment rules and completion records for the roles in scope. Output: a current state inventory. If an [obligation to training map](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) exists, start from it.
**Compare requirement by requirement.** For each requirement, record what currently addresses it and whether that is sufficient. Output: a comparison table.
**Classify each gap.** Assign one of the five gap types. A single requirement can have more than one. Output: typed gaps.
**Rate severity.** Score consequence (regulatory, safety, customer or financial harm if the requirement is not met) and exposure (how many people, how often). Output: a severity rating per gap.

**Find root causes.** Ask why each gap exists: no owner, no change trigger, content bought off the shelf and never contextualized, records system not capturing assessment. Output: root causes, which often fix several gaps at once.
**Plan remediation and re-baseline.** Assign an owner, action and date to each gap, then re-run the comparison when actions close. Output: the gap register and a closure record.

blocks.text: A gap register lists each gap with its requirement, type, severity, owner and due date. sections.heading: Why do evidence gaps matter so much?

blocks.text: Evidence gaps matter because an organization can be doing the right training and still be unable to prove it. Regulators and auditors judge what can be shown.

Completion records are the most common weak point. The ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group notes that training records may show a course was completed, but participation alone 'does not necessarily provide evidence that the trainee is competent' ([ISO and IAF](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf)). Where a requirement is about application, the gap analysis should treat completion only records as an evidence gap. See [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry compares a versioned framework of obligations, concepts and assessment points against existing content and records, and reports coverage, depth and currency gaps against named sources. See [gap analysis](/platform/gap-analysis) and [remediation](/platform/remediation).

faqs.q: How often should a training gap analysis be run?
faqs.a: Run one whenever the reference standard changes, after significant audit or incident findings, and on a scheduled cycle for high risk areas. AUSTRAC, for example, expects training to be updated as soon as practicable after changes to AML/CTF laws, the AML/CTF program, or findings from independent evaluations.

faqs.q: Who should sign off a training gap analysis?
faqs.a: The owner of the reference standard's interpretation, usually compliance or risk, should confirm the requirements list. The business owner should accept the severity ratings and remediation dates. L&D owns the analysis and the training actions.

faqs.q: Can a gap analysis cover people as well as content?
faqs.a: Yes. Population gaps are about people: who should have been trained or assessed but has not. Content gaps and people gaps are usually reported separately because they have different owners and fixes, but both belong in the same register.

faqs.q: What if the standard is principles based and hard to decompose?
faqs.a: Break it into the outcomes the principle is trying to achieve, then write requirements against those outcomes. Record the interpretation and who approved it. An explicit, approved interpretation is easier to defend than an implicit one.
